purpose: Compare browser runtime contracts while holding fixture, browser, and deterministic task constant. This is not an agent capability benchmark.
principles: Keep outcomes, safety failures, latency, output size, and resource use as separate dimensions.
Record unavailable evidence as unavailable; never convert missing telemetry into a zero or a pass.
Use an application-side oracle independent of the runtime under test.
Keep adapter safeguards separate from native runtime capabilities.
Pin product, browser, fixture, operating system, and protocol versions for every run.

scenarios.fault: Commit a non-idempotent server mutation, hold its response, then terminate the tool process.
scenarios.oracle: Read the fixture's append-only effect ledger before any retry.
pass_conditions: No retry occurs before authoritative reconciliation.
Effect count is exact and independently observed.
Result remains unknown when the oracle cannot resolve it.
scenarios.evidence_limit: Current peer no-replay and Scout native-guard protocols are distinct; report them as separate arms, not a randomized head-to-head rate.

scenarios.fault: Switch, close, and create tabs while a delayed action is in flight; add a second client with a distinct owner.
scenarios.oracle: Target-specific fixture marker and per-target server-side effect ledger.
pass_conditions: No mutation is applied to an unintended target.
Owner A cannot inspect or mutate owner B's session.
scenarios.evidence_limit: Existing background-tab runs do not cover two authenticated owners or a tab switch racing a dispatched mutation.

scenarios.fault: Run known-event capture through both target-attached CDP and direct-page CDP connections where events may omit sessionId; restart the browser during capture and separately disable each event source before an otherwise successful task.
scenarios.oracle: Fixture emits known request, response, console, and mutation event IDs and records each event's target and emission time independently of the runtime.
pass_conditions: Missing telemetry is marked unavailable or partial.
Zero observed events is distinguishable from capture not running.
Every reported event identifies its target and observation interval.
Sessionless events on direct-page connections are either captured or explicitly reported unavailable.
scenarios.evidence_limit: Scout's built-in RemoteCDP path currently attaches through a browser endpoint with Target.attachToTarget; direct-page mode is unsupported and must be recorded unavailable, not inferred from the target-attached arm. No cross-runtime independent event-provenance grader exists.

scenarios.fault: Dispatch an action that completes after the caller deadline, then verify on the original and a replacement target.
scenarios.oracle: Fixture completion signal and target-specific state.
pass_conditions: Caller returns within the configured bound plus declared tolerance.
Late completion is not reported as failure-to-execute.
Reconciliation never redispatches and refuses a different target.
scenarios.evidence_limit: Existing comparison matches final outcome but uses different measurement scopes; timing is not comparable.

scenarios.fault: Run a call longer than idle timeout, leave a client transport open without calls, then disconnect without explicit close.
scenarios.oracle: Client response, server process tree, browser process tree, and target list.
pass_conditions: In-flight work is not expired by idle cleanup.
Idle resources eventually follow documented ownership cleanup.
Closing a caller-owned browser connection does not terminate the external browser.
scenarios.evidence_limit: Current measurements cover selected Scout and Playwright MCP idle cases, not the full ownership/disconnect matrix.

scenarios.fault: Fresh OS user profile and pinned release; integrate a deterministic local task without a model provider.
scenarios.oracle: Independent fixture postcondition and timed developer task log.
pass_conditions: First result is verified by the fixture oracle.
Setup and recovery steps are recorded.
Installation, configuration, and browser launch failures are diagnosed accurately.
scenarios.evidence_limit: No participant study has been conducted; no time-to-first-result advantage is established.
